generated_at.note: Declared with --generated-at and recorded in docs/journey_town_input_receipt.json; never read from the clock.

purpose: The real map of Mae Sai town for the /journey/ story: open building outlines, OpenStreetMap roads and water, Copernicus relief and the water of the published September 2024 replay (r5) at the hours of the story. For preparedness learning; the people of the story are fictional.
confidence_reason: Water extents are a terrain-model reconstruction with illustrative stages; the late-recession size was tuned to one radar pass rather than checked independently, and spatial agreement there is weak. Building outlines were drawn by a model on satellite images of earlier years, not surveyed; building heights, floors, facades and trees are illustrative.
assumptions: The water is the published replay r5: a HAND (height above nearest drainage) reconstruction driven by illustrative stage keyframes. A cell is wet when the stage is above code x 0.05 m; its depth is k x (stage - code x 0.05). It is a model, not an observation.
Beat stages are numpy.interp of the r5 stage anchors at hour / 24 (the same values as the app's stageAt); hour 0 is 9 Sep 2024 00:00 ICT.

The local frame is equirectangular at the example home with the constants of groundDistanceM (111320 x cos(20.44042 deg) m per degree of longitude, 110540 m per degree of latitude); x east, z south, y up.

The r5 cells are linear in Web Mercator rows over the manifest's rounded bounds; the affine of the cropped cell centres is a straight-line fit whose largest error is recorded (cells.max_affine_error_m).

Relief of never-flooding cells is the Copernicus DSM (it includes buildings and trees) minus one drainage datum, the median of DSM - k x code x 0.05 over the floodable cells of the detail box, clamped to at least 12.8 m so it stays above the highest floodable cell. Heights are for the scene, not survey levels.

Cover classes come from OpenStreetMap: water (water polygons and river, canal and stream lines at 20, 6 and 4 m), roads (centrelines at their width, at least one 4 m cell wide), buildings (the simplified outlines), green and field land use. Precedence: water > building > road > field > green > open ground. Unmapped land reads as open ground.

Outlines are simplified by 0.35 m (topology kept); slivers under 8 m2 and outlines crossing the box edge are dropped. Kinds follow fixed rules on OpenStreetMap sites, size and distance to main roads; floors come from a hash of the outline: both are illustrative.

Trees are placed by a seeded Poisson-disk sampler (seed 20240909) on river banks, green land, field edges and open ground, at least 2.5 m from buildings and roads: an illustration, not a tree inventory.

The usual walk follows the replay's walking network (outputs/mae_sai_access_edges.csv) from the network node nearest the home to the nearest reported shelter of the reported_2024 set within 2 km. An edge closes at the replay's road rule (sample_road and closure_stage: 10 m samples on the r5 cells, impassable at 0.3 m, channel and never-flood samples ignored); shelters are assumed open for the whole replay. The replay's access sets also drop a shelter once its own site floods; the shelters reachable from the home here never do.
Reported sites come from the replay's compiled list of public reporting (not an official register).
limitations: Not a real-time product or an official warning; for preparedness learning only.
The September 2024 water is a model reconstruction with low confidence: onset and peak extents were not observed.
Building outlines are model-drawn from images of earlier years: buildings may be missing, merged or no longer there.
The outline file covers Thailand only: north of the Sai River (Tachileik, Myanmar) the pack has OpenStreetMap roads but no buildings.
OpenStreetMap land use is sparse in Mae Sai: most fields, orchards and wooded hills are not mapped and read as open ground.
The terrain model is a surface model at 30 m: in town it is biased up by buildings and trees.

The replay's drainage lines (cells of HAND 0, from the 30 m surface model) run about 100 to 150 m south of the mapped Sai River through town (median 115 m from OpenStreetMap water): the replay's water rises from the model's lines, while the river at a dry hour is drawn from OpenStreetMap.
Building outlines overlap where the source does (about 2,600 pairs by more than 1 m2), so some drawn buildings meet or cross.
The walk closures here are read on the 15 m r5 cells; the Public app's cut level comes from the replay's own 10 m grid. They agree within the tolerance recorded in route.app.
No ponding after the river falls: the replay dries every cell as soon as the assumed river level drops below it.
The homes are model points of the replay's resident grid, not addresses; the people of the story are fictional.
The Thai text of this pack was written and checked by the assistant; it has not been reviewed by a native speaker.

frame.axes: x east, z south, y up; metres (places) or integer decimetres (vectors)

cells.affine_rule: Centre of crop cell (c, r): x = x0 + c * dx, z = z0 + r * dz (r5 column col0 + c, row row0 + r).

georef.rule: col = floor((lon - W) / (E - W) * 1610); row = floor((mercY(N) - mercY(lat)) / (mercY(N) - mercY(S)) * 1753); mercY(lat) = ln(tan(pi/4 + lat/2))

channels.R: code: 0 channel, 1-254 effective HAND in 0.05 m steps, 255 never floods
channels.B: 255 where the r5 low-confidence byte >= 128 and the cell is not channel, else 0

relief.encoding: R, G = big-endian uint16 of height_dm + 2000 for cells with code 255, else 0; B = 0 (same cells as the cells PNG)
relief.datum_rule: median over floodable cells (code 1-254, centre inside the detail box) of DSM - k * code * 0.05, rounded to 0.01 m
relief.height_rule: DSM (bilinear at the cell centre) - datum_m, clamped to >= 12.8 m

cover.cell_rule: Centre of cell (c, r): x = x0 + c * cell_m, z = z0 + r * cell_m; a polygon fills the cells whose centre it covers.

rules.water: OSM natural=water, water=*, landuse=reservoir|basin, waterway=riverbank polygons; waterway river, canal, stream lines buffered 10, 3, 2 m each side
rules.road: OSM road centrelines buffered by half their width (at least 2 m, so one cell)
rules.building: the simplified outlines of this pack

backdrop.cell_rule: Centre of cell (c, r): x = x0 + c * cell_m, z = z0 + r * cell_m
backdrop.encoding: R, G = big-endian uint16 of (DSM - datum_m) in decimetres + 2000; B = 0

route.rule: Shortest walk on the replay's network at stage 0 from the node nearest the home to the nearest reported shelter of the reported_2024 set within 2 km. An edge is open while the stage is below its closure stage.
route.closure_rule: closure_stage(sample_road(...)) of floodguard.evacuation_access and scripts/mae_sai_timeline_evacuation.py on samples every 10 m along the edge, read on the r5 cells: the stage at which the depth k x (stage - code x 0.05) first reaches 0.3 m at a usable sample (channel and never-flood samples ignored).

app.home_k_note: home_k is the depth factor x 255 (unscaled, clipped to 1..255), not the hand PNG's byte scale of 2.5.
app.rule: nearestAccessNode (within 150 m, groundDistanceM) of apps/web/src/lib/public-practice.ts; cut code indexes access.levels

buildings.encoding: ring_start[i] is the index of building i's first vertex in the vertex list (length count + 1, the last value is the vertex total); coords holds 2 integers per vertex in decimetres: the first vertex of each ring absolute, the next ones as differences from the previous vertex. Rings are counter-clockwise in the x/z plane (positive shoelace area) and do not repeat the first vertex. Edge i runs from vertex i to i + 1.
kind_rules: temple: representative point inside an OSM amenity=place_of_worship or building=temple|shrine polygon
market: inside amenity=marketplace, or area >= 900 m2 when none of the above
shophouse: within 12 m + half the road width of a trunk, primary, secondary or tertiary centreline (links included)
buildings.floors_rule: lo + h mod (hi - lo + 1), h = first 4 bytes of SHA-256 of the outline id; ranges: shophouse 2-4, house 1-2, large 1-2, shed 1-1, temple 1-1, government 2-3, school 2-3, market 1-1. Illustrative.
buildings.front_rule: edge whose outward normal points most directly at the nearest point of the nearest road; among edges within 0.1 of the best cosine, the longest
buildings.obb_encoding: 5 integers per building: cx_dm, cz_dm, w_dm (side most parallel to the front edge), d_dm, angle of the w side in centidegrees from +x toward +z, 0-17999
buildings.compound_rule: index into places of the reported site whose OSM polygon holds the outline's representative point, else -1
buildings.conf_rule: outline confidence x 100 (Google); -1 where the source gives none (Microsoft)

roads.encoding: line_start[i] is the index of road line i's first vertex (length count + 1); coords as for buildings (first vertex absolute, then differences, decimetres)
roads.width_rule: width tag (m), else lanes x 3.25 m, else the class default: trunk 140, primary 120, secondary 90, tertiary 80, unclassified 60, residential 50, living_street 45, service 35, track 30, path 18, footway 18, pedestrian 18, other 35 (dm)

trees.encoding: coords: 2 integers per tree in decimetres, sorted by z then x, the first absolute and the next ones as differences
trees.scale_rule: percent of the kind's base size, 75-125
trees.rule: Dart-throwing Poisson-disk passes in order (spacing m): river_bank 9 m, at most 900, green 6 m, at most 2000, field_edge 8 m, at most 300, open_ground 16 m, at most 1800; never within 2.5 m of a building or of a road as drawn in the cover raster; river bank = plantable cells within 25 m of water (coconut palms); field edge = field cells next to another class; at most 5000 in all.
